reasoning.text: The render passes both acceptance tests. ISO shows an open, fully populated eight-lane board with no opaque block swallowing a subsystem; TOP confirms eight blue BRAM banks, both white FIFO capsules, the copper DSP multiplier column as a vertical row of dots, the brass twiddle feeder/rail L, the dark reduction spine pair, and the right-edge control cluster; SIDE shows the exploded butterfly lane riding on its two risers and the elevated routing channels; FRONT shows the seven-fin exploded heatsink lifted on its stub. The only real residual defect carried from the prior pass was geometric: of the three overhead routing channels only the return bus was grounded, leaving the brass twiddle broadcast rail and the copper operand-read bus reading as floating lines in the SIDE/FRONT elevations. That is now fixed with two short standoff posts, so all three channels read as physical wiring tied to the array frame.

fields.before: Elevated broadcast rail running the full depth of the multiplier column, fanning the single fetched twiddle factor down to all eight DSP modular multipliers each cycle so each root of unity is read once and reused.
fields.after: Elevated broadcast rail running the full depth of the multiplier column, fanning the single fetched twiddle factor down to all eight DSP modular multipliers each cycle so each root of unity is read once and reused; supported on a central standoff post onto the array frame.

fields.before: Operand-read bus carrying source coefficients fetched conflict-free from the crossbar eastward into the DSP multiplier-column inputs; together with the brass twiddle rail and the blue return bus it makes the full read/twiddle/return dataflow triad visible and is the read half of the read-modify-write loop.
fields.after: Operand-read bus carrying source coefficients fetched conflict-free from the crossbar eastward into the DSP multiplier-column inputs; together with the brass twiddle rail and the blue return bus it makes the full read/twiddle/return dataflow triad visible and is the read half of the read-modify-write loop, supported on a standoff post onto the array frame.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic. 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the forward-NTT input FIFO and the natural-order output FIFO. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the rail spanning the multiplier column so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one butterfly cluster onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (multiply->add/sub->register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the seven-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
